title: Linkability of Student Identity to Assignment Submissions
description: Student's identity (student id) is linked to their assignment submission data (work file, course, timestamp), potentially enabling tracking of student behavior across courses and time periods.
assumptions: Student ID is included in submission data and can be correlated with other data sources.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable fit for linkability concerns in ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Assignment Data
description: Assignment data (work file, student id, course, submission timestamp) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network and stored in the system without adequate access controls.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a reasonable fit for disclosure concerns in ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Usurpation of Student Identity During Login
description: An attacker could potentially usurp a student's identity during the login process, gaining unauthorized access to submit assignments on behalf of the student.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism may have vulnerabilities or weak credentials.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a reasonable fit for usurpation concerns in ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Assignment Submissions
description: Assignment data could be tampered with during processing in the Grades Portal Web App, altering the work file, student id, course, or submission timestamp.
assumptions: System may lack adequate integrity controls or encryption for data in transit and at rest.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a reasonable fit for data integrity concerns in ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, and file reference to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2), creating a flow of identifying information between processes.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the P1→P2 flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.2.1.1 from context applies to identifier threats; confidence in this specific node for Process→Process flow is moderate.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference received from the portal, enabling identification of students through their submissions and grades.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading and record-keeping purposes.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data; confidence moderate for Process→Process context.

title: Non-repudiation of Submission and Grading Requests
description: The flow transmits requesting role and submission data, creating evidence that could prevent students or instructors from denying their involvement in specific grading or submission actions.
assumptions: The system logs and retains evidence of who requested what grading action.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation as a privacy threat (inability to deny) is less common than as a security goal; this is a genuine privacy concern in educational contexts.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure of Student Personal Information
description: The Assignment & Grading Service explicitly stores student ID, course, and submission time in the Assignment Store. This represents an intentional disclosure of personal data by design. The threat concerns whether this data collection is minimal and strictly necessary for the grading function, or if it exceeds what's required for the intended purpose.
assumptions: Student ID is considered personal/identifiable information under privacy regulations

title: Student Identifiability Through Stored Assignment Data
description: The stored assignment data includes student ID, which directly identifies the student. This creates a risk that the assignment data can be used to identify and potentially profile individual students, especially if combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Student ID is a direct identifier that can be used to re-identify individuals

title: Linkability of Assignment Data with Other Student Records
description: The student ID stored in the Assignment Store could potentially be used to link this assignment data with other student records (e.g., grades, personal information, course history), creating a comprehensive profile of the student across multiple systems.
assumptions: Student ID is a common key used across multiple data systems
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether other systems use the same student ID format and whether data is shared across systems

title: Processing of identified student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes student submission data that contains identifiable information (student names, course assignments, grades). When teachers request submission queues, the system processes this identified data, creating privacy risks for students whose data is being accessed.
assumptions: Student submissions contain personally identifiable information that is processed by the system.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student submission data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are not properly enforced. Teachers could potentially access submissions from courses they are not authorized to review, or data could be leaked through improper logging or storage.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly implemented or enforced for submission data access.

title: Teacher identity impersonation during login
description: The teacher's login credentials could be compromised, allowing an attacker to impersonate the teacher and access submission queues they are not authorized to review. This could lead to unauthorized access to student data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential theft or brute force attacks.

title: Student Identifiability in Submission Display
description: Student names and work content are displayed to the teacher, making students directly identifiable through the grades portal.
assumptions: Teacher has access to the portal and can view student submissions with names attached.

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Submissions
description: Student submission data (names, work content, times) could be accessed by unauthorized individuals if the portal lacks proper access controls.
assumptions: Portal may have insufficient authentication or authorization mechanisms protecting student data.

title: Linkability of Student Data Across Systems
description: Student submission data displayed to teachers could be linked to other student records or systems, creating a comprehensive profile of student activities.
assumptions: Student data may be accessible across multiple systems or could be correlated with other data sources.

title: Teacher grading activity linked to student records
description: Teacher's submission of grades and feedback could be linked to student identification data, enabling correlation of teacher actions with specific student records across systems.
assumptions: Teacher has access to student identification data and grading system

title: Student grades and feedback disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Grades, written feedback, and student IDs transmitted to the Grades Portal could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized individuals, violating student privacy expectations.
assumptions: Data transmission lacks adequate encryption or access controls

title: Teacher identity usurped for grade submission
description: An attacker could impersonate the teacher to submit fraudulent grades or feedback, compromising grade integrity and student records.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism is weak or bypassed

title: Student data handling may violate privacy regulations
description: Collection and transmission of student grades, feedback, and IDs may not comply with FERPA, GDPR, or other educational privacy regulations depending on jurisdiction and data retention policies.
assumptions: Institution lacks proper compliance framework for student data
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction; this is a general concern

title: Teacher identified through grader ID in submitted data
description: The grader ID included in the data flow could be used to identify the specific teacher responsible for grading, potentially exposing teacher identity in student records.
assumptions: Grader ID is not anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The grading service writing to the Grade Records Database could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive student grades and personal information.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls on the database or network transmission
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node for Process→DataStore flows

title: Student and Grader Identification
description: Grade records contain student id and grader id, which could be used to identify specific individuals and their academic performance.
assumptions: Student and grader IDs are not properly anonymized or protected
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a representative identification threat node

title: Linkability of Student Data
description: Grade records could be linked with other student data (e.g., enrollment records, personal information) to create comprehensive profiles of students.
assumptions: Student IDs are used consistently across multiple systems without proper isolation
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a representative linkability threat node

title: Grade Record Tampering
description: Grade records could be altered or corrupted during the write operation, potentially changing grades or feedback without proper audit trails.
assumptions: Insufficient integrity controls or audit logging on the database
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a representative data degradation threat node

title: Database-Level Unauthorized Disclosure
description: The Grade Records Database itself could be accessed by unauthorized entities, exposing all stored grade records.
assumptions: Database lacks proper access controls, encryption, or audit mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node for DataStore

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Storage of student grades and personal information may violate data protection regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper safeguards are not implemented.
assumptions: Data handling practices may not meet legal requirements for educational data
uncertainty_note: Using Nc.1.1 as a representative non-compliance threat node

title: Processing of identified student grades data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified personal data (student grades and feedback) that can be linked to the specific student EE1. This processing of identified data creates privacy risks as the system handles sensitive academic information.
assumptions: The system processes grades that are personally identifiable to the student

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: There is a risk that student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data leaks, or unauthorized system access during the grade retrieval process.
assumptions: The system may have vulnerabilities in access control mechanisms

title: Student identity usurpation during grade access
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the student (EE1) to access their grades and feedback, either through credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering attacks.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to identity spoofing

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades During Transmission
description: Grades and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during data flow, potentially exposing sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Network vulnerabilities or inadequate encryption could allow interception of data in transit.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard web portal without explicit mention of encryption mechanisms.

title: Linkability of Grades to Student Identity
description: Student grades displayed in the portal could be linked to the student's identity, potentially enabling correlation with other data sources to build comprehensive profiles.
assumptions: Grades are displayed with student identifiers that could be used for correlation.
uncertainty_note: Assuming grades are displayed in a way that maintains student anonymity within the portal context.

title: Account Compromise Leading to Unauthorized Grade Access
description: If a student's account credentials are compromised, unauthorized parties could access the student's grades and teacher feedback through the portal.
assumptions: Weak authentication or credential theft could allow unauthorized access to student accounts.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard authentication mechanisms without additional security controls mentioned.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's grades to third parties
description: Parent's account credentials could be compromised, allowing unauthorized parties to access and view the child's grades through the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Parent account credentials are stored or transmitted insecurely; third parties may attempt to intercept or steal credentials.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard disclosure threat node; confidence in applicability is high based on flow context.

title: Parent account impersonation during login
description: An attacker could impersonate the parent during the login process, gaining unauthorized access to the child's grades and potentially other sensitive information.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism may be vulnerable to credential theft, phishing, or session hijacking.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a standard usurpation threat node; confidence in applicability is high for login flows.

title: Inappropriate data disclosure to unauthorized users
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose child's grades to users without proper authorization verification, even if they have a parent account.
assumptions: Access control mechanisms may be insufficient; parent-child account linking may not be properly enforced.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.2 is a standard disclosure threat node; confidence in applicability is high for process-level data handling.

title: Grade data integrity compromise
description: Grades could be tampered with or altered by unauthorized actors within the Grades Portal Web App, leading to inaccurate records.
assumptions: Data integrity controls may be insufficient; lack of proper audit trails or validation mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard integrity threat node; confidence in applicability is moderate as integrity threats are less common than disclosure threats in this context.

title: Non-repudiation of grade access or modification
description: Parents or administrators may be unable to prove that they accessed or modified grades, leading to disputes over accountability.
assumptions: System may lack proper logging, audit trails, or cryptographic proof mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nr.1.1 is a standard non-repudiation threat node; confidence in applicability is moderate as this is a secondary concern compared to disclosure and access threats.

title: Linkability of grades data to other child information
description: Parent may link the displayed grades, feedback, and submission history to other information about the child (e.g., from other systems or personal knowledge), creating a comprehensive profile of the child's academic performance and behavior.
assumptions: Parent has access to other data sources about the child or can infer connections through the grades data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades data
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data logging mechanisms that expose sensitive academic information.
assumptions: System has vulnerabilities or inadequate access controls that could expose data to unauthorized entities.

title: Usurpation of parent identity to access grades
description: An unauthorized third party may usurp the parent's identity to access the child's grades, feedback, and submission history through credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be compromised or social engineering attacks are possible.

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations for student data
description: The system may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding the collection, display, and transmission of student grades and academic information to parents.
assumptions: System may not have proper compliance controls or documentation for regulatory requirements.

title: Administrator Account Impersonation
description: School Administrator (EE4) could be impersonated by an attacker gaining unauthorized access to the Grades Portal Web App, allowing them to create, modify, or disable accounts and parent-child links on behalf of the legitimate administrator.
assumptions: Administrator credentials are compromised or weak authentication is in place

title: Sensitive PII Disclosure via Administrator Actions
description: Administrator's ability to create, modify, and disable accounts exposes sensitive PII (names, emails, roles, relationships) to unauthorized disclosure if access controls are insufficient or if administrator actions are not properly logged/audited.
assumptions: Administrator has broad access to sensitive student/parent data

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Administrative Actions
description: Administrator actions (creating/modifying accounts, parent-child links) may lack proper audit trails, allowing the administrator to deny performing specific actions that could impact student/parent records.
assumptions: Insufficient logging or audit mechanisms for administrative operations

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Account/Relationship Data
description: Grades Portal Web App (P1) could have data integrity issues when processing administrator modifications to accounts and parent-child links, potentially leading to corrupted or inconsistent relationship data.
assumptions: Input validation or data processing errors in the web application

title: Linkability of Administrator Actions to Student/Parent Records
description: Administrator's actions (creating/modifying accounts) could be linked to specific student/parent records, potentially revealing patterns about administrative behavior or creating audit trails that could be exploited.
assumptions: System logs or metadata could be correlated to identify administrator actions

title: Unauthorized disclosure of account records to the directory
description: The grading service writes account records to the account directory, which may be accessible to unauthorized users or systems, leading to potential data leakage of student and parent information.
assumptions: The account directory has access controls that may not be properly enforced or may be bypassed.

title: Unauthorized modification of account records and parent-child links
description: An attacker could modify account records or parent-child relationship links in the account directory, potentially altering student records or family connections.
assumptions: The account directory lacks adequate integrity controls or authentication mechanisms.

title: Identification of students and family members through stored records
description: Account records containing parent-child relationships could be used to identify students and their family members, potentially revealing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The account records contain personally identifiable information that can be linked to real individuals.

title: Usurpation of grading service identity in account directory
description: An attacker could impersonate the grading service and write fraudulent account records or modify existing records to appear as if they originated from the legitimate grading service.
assumptions: The grading service lacks proper authentication or digital signatures for its operations.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) transfers full grade records, assignments, and account directory to the Cloud Hosting Provider (EE5) as part of nightly backup and replication. This constitutes an explicit disclosure of personal data across a system boundary to a known third party.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider has access to and processes the transferred data; the transfer is intentional and by design.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 selected based on context [5] describing data disclosure as transfer to third party; exact node numbering may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Linkability of Student Records via Cloud Transfer
description: Grade records, assignments, and account directory transferred to the cloud provider may be linked to identify specific students/users, potentially enabling correlation of data across systems or time.
assumptions: The cloud provider maintains the data in a way that preserves identifiers; data may be accessible to other systems or personnel.
uncertainty_note: Linkability threat inferred from the nature of transferred data containing PII; exact tree node may need verification.

title: Unauthorized Access to Transferred Student Data
description: The transferred grade records, assignments, and account directory may be accessed by unauthorized parties at the cloud hosting provider or through compromised cloud infrastructure.
assumptions: Cloud provider security controls may be insufficient; data in transit or at rest may be vulnerable.
uncertainty_note: Usurpation threat based on standard cloud security risks; specific provider security posture unknown.

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Individuals
description: Grade records in DS2 can be linked to specific students, parents, and teachers through the Assignment & Grading Service, potentially enabling correlation of data across different views and contexts.
assumptions: The grading service maintains records that can be cross-referenced with other data sources

title: Identification of Students and Parents from Grade Records
description: Grade records in DS2 contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify specific students and their parents, especially when combined with the views built by the grading service.
assumptions: Grade records include student identifiers and parent contact information

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grade Records
description: Grade records from DS2 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the flow to P2, potentially exposing sensitive academic and personal information to individuals without proper access rights.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly enforced during data retrieval

title: Usurpation of Student or Parent Identity
description: An attacker could impersonate a student, parent, or teacher to access grade records through the Assignment & Grading Service, potentially gaining unauthorized access to sensitive educational information.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to identity spoofing
